- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope after peak.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.3) and model forecast is flat or declining, model underestimates bullish momentum; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.1–0.3) and price is trending sideways, model often overfits recent noise; apply mean reversion by smoothing forecast toward 14-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates volatility in early days; cap forecast variance within ±1.5x recent 7-day range to avoid extreme outliers.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often underestimates depth of decline; add 1–2% buffer below true low to avoid premature bottoming.
